The service shall be an OpenID Connect provider built on `oidc-provider` 9.x with a PostgreSQL adapter implementing all seven adapter methods
The service shall publish `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and a JWKS endpoint
The service shall support only the authorization code grant with PKCE `S256`, for every client type
Authorization codes shall be single-use; replay shall revoke every token derived from that code
`redirect_uri` and `post_logout_redirect_uri` shall match a registered value exactly; no wildcards
The service shall sign tokens only with asymmetric keys (ES256 default, RS256 available), include `kid`, and never accept `alg=none`
The authorization response shall include `iss` (RFC 9207)
Access tokens shall be opaque with a 10-minute lifetime
Refresh tokens shall rotate on every use with a 30-day absolute lifetime, and reuse of a rotated token shall revoke the grant family
The service shall implement RP-Initiated Logout requiring `id_token_hint` and a pre-registered post-logout URI
The service shall implement Back-Channel Logout with signed logout tokens (`sid`, `sub`, `events`, `jti`, `exp` ≤ 2 min) sent on logout, suspension, grant revocation and revoke-all
Back-channel delivery shall retry three times and then mark the app *slow revoke* and write an audit event
The service shall expose `userinfo` returning standard claims plus `roles` for the token's client
The service shall not implement dynamic client registration, WebFinger, implicit, password or `client_credentials` grants
Confidential clients shall authenticate at the token endpoint with `client_secret_basic`; secrets ≥ 256 bits, hashed at rest, shown once
Public native clients shall be supported with custom-scheme and loopback redirects per RFC 8252, no secret
The ID token shall carry `sub`, `email`, `email_verified`, `preferred_username`, `name`, `auth_time`, `amr`, `sid`, and `roles` when `d3:roles` is requested
Tokens shall tolerate ±60 s clock skew
The provider shall run with `provider.proxy = true` and compute `https://auth.d3cloud.io` as issuer behind the tunnel
Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628)
Email shall be the unique, case-insensitive login identifier
Each user shall have a stable, unique username exposed as `preferred_username`, never derived from email
`sub` shall be an opaque UUIDv7 per user, identical across all clients
Passwords shall be hashed with Argon2id at ≥ 19 MiB / t=2 / p=1 plus a pepper from the environment
Password policy: ≥ 12 characters, rejected if in a common/breached list that includes entries ≥ 12 chars, no composition rules, no expiry, checked at set time only
Unknown-email login attempts shall perform a decoy hash so timing is indistinguishable
Per-account throttling: 4 free attempts then doubling delay to a 10-minute cap, evaluated before hashing, never a hard lockout, reset works while throttled
Per-IP throttling keyed on `CF-Connecting-IP`: 20 free attempts then doubling delay
Login shall be a state machine whose only terminal state completes the interaction; there shall be no boolean MFA-pending flag
SSO session: 30-day remember-me, `__Host-` cookie, `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`, regenerated at login and privilege change
Every interaction form POST shall carry a CSRF token
The login screen shall present an email field and a prominent *Sign in with a passkey* control supporting discoverable credentials and conditional UI; the password step follows email entry
TOTP enrolment (QR + manual key + confirm) and verification with ±1 step window, single-use via last-used-step tracking
Passkey registration and authentication via `@simplewebauthn/server` with an opaque random `webauthn_user_id`, RP ID `auth.d3cloud.io`, counter and `backedUp` stored

Second factor optional for guests; mandatory for owner and admins as *any* factor with user verification (passkey UV or TOTP); the API shall refuse admin grant to an account with zero verified factors
Trusted device: after a successful second factor the user may opt into a signed 30-day device cookie that skips MFA; listed and revocable
Owner-only console actions shall require a second-factor step-up within the last 5 minutes
Users shall have states `invited → active → suspended`; suspension revokes sessions and sends back-channel logout
Admin-initiated reset shall clear password and all factors, revoke sessions and trusted devices, send back-channel logouts, and email a re-enrol link
`email_verified` shall be true only after the user proves mailbox control (invite acceptance or verification link) and shall flip to false when an admin edits the address
The trusted-device and session cookies shall never be issued to a suspended user
Removing the last verified factor from an owner or admin shall be refused
Per-app MFA requirement via `acr_values`
Per-user recovery codes
Sessions shall record IP, user agent, created, last-seen, expiry, revoked
Apps shall be registered from a JSON manifest (client id, name, type, redirect URIs, post-logout URIs, back-channel URI, roles) via console or seed file only
Roles shall be declared by the app manifest with key, display name, description, sort order and optional default; the console shall not create roles outside a manifest
Re-registering a manifest shall diff roles and block removal of a role currently granted unless confirmed
A grant shall associate one user with one app and a set of that app's roles
Effective roles shall be the union of direct-grant roles and group-grant roles for that app
An authorization request by a user with no grant for the client shall end in `access_denied` before any consent or interstitial and write an audit event
The `roles` claim shall contain only the requesting client's effective roles and shall be omitted unless `d3:roles` is requested
Groups shall exist with members and group grants (group × app × roles); groups shall never appear in tokens or userinfo
Disabling an app shall reject new authorizations and revoke its tokens
Client secrets shall be rotatable; the new secret is shown once
Grant creation, change and revocation shall trigger back-channel logout for that user × app
The seed file `d3auth.seed.json` shall register apps and roles idempotently on boot
The system shall store no organisation/tenant assumption that would block adding one later (no global-unique names beyond email/username/client id)
A first-party interstitial *Continue to {app} as {username}* shall be shown on a user's first login to each app, with a *Not you?* switch
